situation: Two students measure the temperature at school at the same time. Ali puts his thermometer in the sun on a concrete floor and reads 45°C. Bouba hangs his in the shade of a tree and reads 34°C.
Their teacher says that neither reading is the official air temperature. The students do not understand how the temperature should be measured.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that the students do not know how to measure the official temperature of the air.
Why did Ali's thermometer show a higher temperature?
It was in direct sunlight and on concrete, which absorbs and gives off a lot of heat.
What can the students do to get a correct reading?
They should place the thermometer in the shade, off the ground, where air can move freely, as in a Stevenson screen.
end.justification: This lesson will help us to measure temperature correctly and to present temperature data.

qa.q: What do we measure when we say how hot or cold the air is?
qa.a: We measure the atmospheric temperature, the degree of hotness or coldness of the air.

sum.title: I. Meaning
defs: Atmospheric temperature is the degree of hotness or coldness of the air. It is measured in degrees Celsius (°C).

qa.q: This thermometer records the highest and the lowest temperature of the day. What is it called?
qa.a: It is called Six's maximum and minimum thermometer. Its two small indices stay at the highest and lowest temperatures reached.

qa.q: In Garoua, the maximum temperature of a day is 38°C and the minimum is 24°C. Calculate the mean daily temperature and the daily range.
How can temperature data for a place or a region be presented?
qa.a: It can be presented in tables, in line graphs, and on maps with isotherms.

sum.title: II. Measurement and Presentation
sum.intro: Temperature is measured and presented in the following ways:
items: The ordinary thermometer gives the temperature at a given time. Six's maximum and minimum thermometer records the highest and lowest temperatures of the day.
– Annual range = mean of the hottest month − mean of the coldest month
Temperature data is presented in tables, line graphs and maps with isotherms, lines joining places with the same temperature.

qa.q: Look at the diagram. Why is the Stevenson screen painted white and why does it have louvred sides?
qa.a: It is painted white to reflect sunlight. Its louvred sides let air flow freely but keep out sunlight and rain.

qa.title: Question 2
qa.q: Give two rules for siting the Stevenson screen.
qa.a: It must stand on short grass, in an open space far from trees and buildings, with the thermometers about 1.25 m above the ground and the door facing north.

sum.title: III. The Stevenson Screen
defs: The Stevenson screen is a white wooden box on legs, with louvred sides, in which thermometers are kept to measure the temperature of the air in the shade.
items: It is painted white to reflect sunlight, has louvred sides for free air flow, a double roof and stands on legs.
– It is placed on short grass, not on concrete.
– It is in an open space, far from trees and buildings.
– The thermometers are about 1.25 m above the ground.
– In the Northern Hemisphere, the door faces north.

evaluation: A day has a maximum of 36°C and a minimum of 22°C. Calculate the daily range.
Why must the Stevenson screen not be placed on concrete?
Concrete absorbs and gives off a lot of heat, so the reading would be too high.
Six's thermometer records the maximum and minimum temperatures of the day.
remediation: The thermometer that records the highest and lowest temperatures is ______'s thermometer.
The white box that protects thermometers is the ______ screen.
Its sides are ______ to let air circulate.
In the Northern Hemisphere, its door faces ______.
end.homework: Wet a piece of cloth and hang it outside in the morning and in the afternoon. Note how long it takes to dry each time.
end.homeworkTag: This prepares Lesson 33: Other Weather Elements (humidity, wind, pressure, sunshine).
teacherNote: WMO standards place thermometers between 1.25 m and 2 m above the ground; 1.25 m is the traditional British standard used in textbooks.
In Six's thermometer, read the end of each index nearest to the mercury.
